critical_findings.finding: capture_job keeps the first capture/spawn/resource failure only in local error, then executes selector.close, each stream.close, each raw-fd fsync/close without independent guards. One cleanup exception replaces the primary, skips remaining closes and prevents JOB_CAPTURE_TERMINAL recording.
critical_findings.static_counterexample: A cap+1 Refusal occurs at436, setting error. The first raw-fd os.fsync at450 raises OSError. That OSError escapes finally before result451 or ledger458; the cap cause is lost to main, remaining closes are skipped and terminal accounting does not exist.
critical_findings.smallest_correction: Treat every acquired handle as owned. Preserve primary error before cleanup, attempt every cleanup operation independently, append secondary errors without replacing primary, retain terminal/unknown-bill evidence even if ledger/writer fails. A secondary reporting failure cannot be represented as a successful cleanup or zero cost.

critical_findings.finding: main disables/restores its timer, then ledger.close can raise and override a prior return or QUEUE_STOP error. Ledger.close itself skips os.close if fsync raises. Final close work is outside the internal alarm and final successful elapsed record precedes it.
critical_findings.static_counterexample: After a failed job records QUEUE_STOP, final ledger fsync raises. The caller sees that new error instead of the retained job primary, and explicit descriptor close is skipped. On a nominal path the emitted success/return decision also precedes a failing close.
critical_findings.smallest_correction: Preserve primary and secondary finalization outcomes, attempt close even after fsync failure, and bind finalization/unknown tail to genuine parent accounting and an actual outer whole-job guard. Do not claim a final successful disposition before required finalization is disposed.

critical_findings.finding: Popen PIPE handles are not added to streams until after fallible ledger.add(SPAWN_RETURNED). If that ledger write fails, returned proc stdout/stderr exist but are absent from the explicit close loop.
critical_findings.static_counterexample: Popen returns the process and two pipes; ledger.add at416 raises. cleanup(proc) is attempted, but streams remains empty, so neither acquired pipe is explicitly closed by the stream loop.
critical_findings.smallest_correction: Register ownership of both returned pipe handles immediately after Popen and before any fallible logging/register operation, or close proc.stdout/stderr independently in finally regardless of streams registration; preserve all first/secondary outcomes.
